tail: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a production sprite sheet of exactly TWO animation frames of a golden meteor FALLING TRAIL ONLY, arranged in a precise 2 columns by 1 row equal-size grid on a fully transparent background. Reference image is STYLE AND PALETTE ONLY: match its warm yellow gold, amber shading, broad hand-painted cel-shaded cartoon shapes for a cute SD fantasy game. Do NOT draw the reference rock or any meteor body. Each cell contains one upright elongated flame/energy trail, meteor travels STRAIGHT DOWN, so a rounded wide luminous attachment base is at bottom and flame tongues taper UPWARD. Cream-yellow hot core at lower center, golden yellow body, orange amber flame edges, 3 or 4 long pointed upward tongues. Subtle warm dark contour, clean readable shapes, limited bloom, no smoke cloud. Two consecutive flicker poses of the SAME trail with identical base width, total height and bottom attachment position, only flame tongue bends and inner light flow change. Both frames equally strong: frame A and B loop seamlessly. Each cell trail stays inside central 65% cell width and 80% cell height, generous transparent margin, NO cross-cell particles. Bottom attachment center at local x=50%, y=85% of EACH cell, top around y=10%. Shape length about twice base width. Entire sheet landscape 2:1, exact equal square cells. No labels, numbers, panel lines, divider, border, text, watermark, no ground, no explosion, no rock, no cast shadow. Genuine transparent alpha, not a painted checkerboard. These are two isolated separate sprites, NOT a single wide illustration.
impact: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a production sprite sheet of exactly FOUR consecutive animation frames of a golden meteor LANDING IMPACT explosion, arranged precise 2 columns x 2 rows of equal square cells, chronological reading left-to-right top-to-bottom. Transparent background. Reference image is STYLE AND PALETTE ONLY: match broad chunky cel-shaded yellow gold, rich amber and cream highlights, cute SD fantasy game hand-painted cartoon aesthetic, readable at small game scale. Do NOT draw a whole meteor rock. A fast ground impact burst throwing golden rock fragments and warm ochre dust outwards. View front three-quarter from slightly above, ground shock ring is a flattened horizontal ellipse, not a front-facing circular portal. The SAME fixed ground impact origin in EVERY cell at local x=50%, y=72%, with exact same ground baseline. Never recenter individual poses as the burst expands. Frame 1 TOP LEFT: compact extremely bright cream-yellow angular impact flash, a tiny flat golden ring, small beginning upward spike; width 30%, height 30%. Frame 2 TOP RIGHT: strongest full broad golden explosion, jagged upward flame-like impact spikes, a wide flattened ground ring and a few chunky gold chips flung sideways, cream core; occupies width 78%, height 60%, entire effect within cell with margins. Frame 3 BOTTOM LEFT: impact light collapses, widened broken low ring, 5-7 gold fragments continuing outward and down, separated rounded amber dust puffs, open transparent center, lower and dimmer than frame 2. Frame 4 BOTTOM RIGHT: visibly near-vanished effect, just a few small faint amber dust wisps and tiny dim settled chips, widely spaced and low to the SAME baseline, no bright center, no large ring, no fresh explosion. Four genuinely different temporal stages, NOT four similar full explosions. Crisp readable edges with restrained soft dust alpha, no black smoky cloud, no environment, no floor plane, no permanent crater, no whole meteor, no labels, text, numbering, divider, grid lines, border or watermark. All effects fully contained in own cell with at least 10% clear outer margins, no cross-cell particles. Actual transparent alpha background, never draw checkerboard. Square overall sheet, exactly four equal square cells.
